Flooding along Danube Disrupts Hungarian Electric Utilities Operations

Severe flooding along the Danube River has caused significant disruptions to Hungary’s electric utilities sector, with multiple power generation and transmission sites affected as water levels continue to rise. MVM Energetika Zrt confirmed that its Dunamenti power plant near Százhalombatta has reduced output since Tuesday after floodwaters breached protective barriers and inundated access roads.

According to the Hungarian Association of Electric Utilities, at least three substations along the riverbanks have been temporarily shut down as a precautionary measure. Several high-voltage transmission routes are currently inaccessible to maintenance crews due to submerged roads, raising concerns about the reliability of supply should the situation worsen.

“We are working around the clock to safeguard critical infrastructure and limit the impact on electricity delivery,” said László Török, spokesperson for MVM Energetika Zrt. “However, with water levels still rising and forecasts predicting further rainfall, the risk of extended disruptions cannot be ruled out.”

Initial reports indicate that the flooding has not yet caused widespread power outages, but grid operators are warning of possible service interruptions if access to key sites does not improve soon. The National Electric Grid Supervisory Board stated that contingency plans are being implemented, including rerouting electricity supplies and preparing mobile generators for deployment near at-risk substations.

Local union representatives have expressed concern about worker safety, noting that crews are facing hazardous conditions while attempting to reinforce flood defences. “The safety of our members is the top priority,” said Attila Szabó, union leader at the Dunamenti facility.

Authorities and utility firms continue to monitor the situation as the Danube remains above danger level.
